### 2012–2018: _The Sticks_, _Very Good Bad Thing_, and _No Culture_
was released on July 17.[[11]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-exclaim-july-16-11) They performed this song on their Canadian tour in 2012, playing in hometown Vancouver on December 19.
In 2014, the band signed with Universal Music Canada to produce their fifth album, _Very Good Bad Thing_, which was released on November 4, 2014. The first single from the album, "Get Out the Way" was released on July 15, 2014.[[12]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-exclaim-July-15-12) The album contains 10 tracks and 2 bonus tracks: "No One To Nothing" and "Jump the Fence."

### 2012–2018: _The Sticks_, _Very Good Bad Thing_, and _No Culture_
Mother Mother played the City of Brampton, Ontario's New Year's festivities at the end of 2016. On November 25, 2016, the band announced their Canadian No Culture Tour. Their tour began in New Brunswick in February 2017 and ended in British Columbia at the end of March 2017.[[13]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-13)

### 2012–2018: _The Sticks_, _Very Good Bad Thing_, and _No Culture_
On February 10, 2017, their sixth album _No Culture_ was released.[[14]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-14) The lead single from the album, "The Drugs", was released on November 4, 2016.[[15]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-15)

### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
[edit]
On November 2, 2018, the band released their seventh studio album _Dance and Cry_.[[16]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-16) The first single from the album, "Get Up", was released on September 14, 2018.[[17]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-17) The band supported the album with the Dance and Cry tour, playing 26 shows across North America, starting on February 7, 2019, in Vancouver and ending March 16, 2019, in Buffalo, New York.[[18]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-18) The tour included a sold out show at New York's Gramercy Theatre.

### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
Starting in late 2020, songs from their 2008 album, _O My Heart_, went viral on the video-sharing platform TikTok, causing their music to reach new streaming highs. The songs, in particular "Hayloft", "Arms Tonite", "Wrecking Ball" and "Burning Pile", became popular, with videos including cosplay and gothic fashion. Although no particular event caused the surge, the band's music did resonate with non-binary communities, as users played Mother Mother songs while discussing gender-related topics.
> Lead vocalist, Ryan Guldemond, described the surge as a"high honor and huge compliment whenever it's suggested that our music might serve as an adequate soundtrack to a courageous journey of self-discovery that often rubs against societal norms". Guldemond further reiterated that their early music "really struggled to fit neatly into the industry standards of either a rock or pop format [...] I sang straight from my throat and had a much more androgynous tone. It was very rich with unisexual harmonies, as well as eccentric, quirky, daring lyrics. Perhaps it's just the right time for people to understand that music".[[1]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-TikTok-1)

### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
due for release on June 25 on Warner Brothers Music.[[20]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-20) The band also released a video for "I Got Love" made up of clips sent in by fans.[[21]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-21) They released their following single from _Inside_, "Sick of the Silence", on June 10, 2021.[[22]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-22) Alongside the release of _Inside_, the band announced the Canadian leg of the Inside tour, which began on December 2, 2021, in Vancouver and ended on May 20, 2022,

### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
in Ottawa.[[23]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-23)
The band released the deluxe version of _Inside_ on January 28, 2022. It included the single, "Life," a sequel to their most popular song "Hayloft," a piano demo for the song "Like A Child" from the main album, and four other new songs.

# Last Music Video Before Disbanding Mother Child Tragedy
[[](https://www.instagram.com/ghibli84) ghibli84 1,294 My debut album is now available online. Check my webpage for more details. It's been a long journey making this album happen. I stop and think of the many roads that led me here. From my naive and sometimes failed attempts of understanding what it meant to be a musician years ago, to finding new scope and understanding — friends, musicians and dedication helping me shape today's strength and knowledge. An album is a stepping stone, it's the honoring of one of the many landscape any musician arrives to, in our ever lasting path of growth — before venturing ahead and keep exploring. This recording would never have happened without my friend Sarah Grohnert, whose serendipitous connection with Teldex Studio in Berlin opened the door to this project. Nor without the support and care of the many friends who held me close in the year following David’s passing. My small suite In Memoriam honours him, while the rest of the programme reflects the landscape I arrived to back then — and tell in their own way different stories of our human condition. I am also deeply grateful to pianist Katherine Austin, whose unwavering support, knowledge, and belief have meant more to me than I can express. People say it takes courage to be vulnerable, but it also takes the care of others — those who hold that vulnerability and help transform it into strength. Those who believe in us. To all the ones who have done that over the years, thank you. Without you, the countless "no's", the unaccessible and closed doors, the constant doubts, would have made me crumble and give up many many years ago already. This album might be a pebble in the ocean, but I am proud of the journey it represents. I hope you will enjoy listening to it. Recorded at Teldex Studio in Berlin and released by @rattlemusicnz, it brings together the monumental Bach–Busoni Chaconne in D minor, my own suite In Memoriam, and music by Chopin: Ballades Nos. 2 & 4 and the Nocturne Op. 27 No. 1. IN MEMORIAM was officially launched at my Auckland Town Hall recital on 29th March.

### 2005–2006: Early career, _Mother_
The five members started off playing under the name Mother, and in the fall of 2005, they independently released a self-titled album. This debut album was recorded with Howard Redekopp, who had also worked with the New Pornographers and Tegan and Sara. When the _Vancouver Province_ rated Mother as one of the top five BC bands to watch for in 2007, they began to receive acclaim for their debut album. Shortly thereafter, Mother landed a nationally broadcast concert opening_[when?_] for [K'naan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K'naan "K'naan") and the [Wailin' Jennys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wailin'_Jennys "The Wailin' Jennys"). In the summer of 2006, they opened for the Australian band The Cat Empire at the sold-out Vancouver International Jazz Festival. Later that year, they made their debut in central Canada at the Montreal International Jazz Festival on June 29 as well as in Toronto on July 1, Canada Day, at the Harbourfront Centre.[[5]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-star-2006-6)

### 2006–2012: _Touch Up_, _O My Heart_, and _Eureka_
[edit]
In October 2006, after playing a set at the Pop Montreal festival, Mother met with Last Gang Records and later signed a four-album contract. At that point, the label encouraged the band to change their name to avoid legal issues, and they renamed themselves Mother Mother. On February 20, 2007, the band re-released its debut album under the new name, renaming the album _Touch Up_ and including two new songs, as well as artwork and overdubs different from the original.
The band released their second album, _O My Heart_, in 2008. Later that year, on December 3, it was announced that Debra-Jean Creelman had left Mother Mother;[[7]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-Myspace-7) on January 26, 2009, the band announced the addition of a new singer/keyboardist, Jasmin Parkin.

On November 2, 2018, the band released their seventh studio album _Dance and Cry_.[[16]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-16) The first single from the album, "Get Up", was released on September 14, 2018.[[17]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-17) The band supported the album with the Dance and Cry tour, playing 26 shows across North America, starting on February 7, 2019, in Vancouver and ending March 16, 2019, in Buffalo, New York.[[18]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-18) The tour included a sold out show at New York's Gramercy Theatre.
texts.13:
### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
Starting in late 2020, songs from their 2008 album, _O My Heart_, went viral on the video-sharing platform TikTok, causing their music to reach new streaming highs. The songs, in particular "Hayloft", "Arms Tonite", "Wrecking Ball" and "Burning Pile", became popular, with videos including cosplay and gothic fashion. Although no particular event caused the surge, the band's music did resonate with non-binary communities, as users played Mother Mother songs while discussing gender-related topics.
> Lead vocalist, Ryan Guldemond, described the surge as a"high honor and huge compliment whenever it's suggested that our music might serve as an adequate soundtrack to a courageous journey of self-discovery that often rubs against societal norms". Guldemond further reiterated that their early music "really struggled to fit neatly into the industry standards of either a rock or pop format [...] I sang straight from my throat and had a much more androgynous tone. It was very rich with unisexual harmonies, as well as eccentric, quirky, daring lyrics. Perhaps it's just the right time for people to understand that music".[[1]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-TikTok-1)
Although the band had not planned on making new music, in October 2020, they stated to _Rolling Stone_ that they were completing their eighth album at The Warehouse Studio in Vancouver.
texts.14:
### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
Dubbed a "pandemic album", it would contain the "energy from the earlier catalog".[[1]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-TikTok-1) On March 9, 2021, Mother Mother released the singles "I Got Love" and "Stay Behind".[[19]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-19) On April 8, 2021, Mother Mother announced their eighth studio album _Inside_,
texts.15:
### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
due for release on June 25 on Warner Brothers Music.[[20]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-20) The band also released a video for "I Got Love" made up of clips sent in by fans.[[21]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-21) They released their following single from _Inside_, "Sick of the Silence", on June 10, 2021.[[22]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-22) Alongside the release of _Inside_, the band announced the Canadian leg of the Inside tour, which began on December 2, 2021, in Vancouver and ended on May 20, 2022,
texts.16:
### 2018–2022: _Dance and Cry_ and _Inside_
in Ottawa.[[23]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVwHMngEZDms2NTfygh0XMnHleYNfvF4oYMjk4lkoee27yEGzU2gh2qqR8LRMq_1CuPLCoTyq8Ikqc5uFV_U7DkLg5H2lZWPSFdDSDsJfaw3UAQ7s77eox6In9qivpqIuclQ#cite_note-23)
The band released the deluxe version of _Inside_ on January 28, 2022. It included the single, "Life," a sequel to their most popular song "Hayloft," a piano demo for the song "Like A Child" from the main album, and four other new songs.

Armored Saint is an American heavy metal band formed in Los Angeles, California, in 1982. Known for their powerful sound and relentless energy, the band gained recognition as one of the standout acts of the 1980s metal scene. Despite facing challenges, including lineup changes and the tragic loss of guitarist Dave Prichard in 1990, they persevered and solidified their legacy.

Led by John Bush (vocals) and Joey Vera (bass), along with Phil Sandoval (guitar), Jeff Duncan (guitar), and Gonzo Sandoval (drums), Armored Saint has released eight studio albums, including the highly acclaimed Symbol of Salvation (1991), Win Hands Down (2015), and Punching the Sky (2020). They are known for their dynamic live performances and have toured with major acts such as Metallica, Judas Priest, and Dio.
After briefly disbanding in 1992 when John Bush joined Anthrax, Armored Saint reunited in 1999 and has remained active ever since. Their music blends classic heavy metal with intricate melodies and powerful storytelling, earning them a dedicated following.
In recent years, they have continued to tour, record, and evolve, with a new album currently in the works as of 2024. Their resilience and commitment to authentic heavy metal make them a revered name in the genre.
